chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about raisins: Is it permissible to cook them until their flavor is extracted, then take that water and cook it until two-thirds evaporate and one-third remains, then let it cool and drink it over the course of a year? He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.السَّنَةَ: The year (over the course of a year)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to boil raisins, reduce the water, and drink the resulting syrup over a year?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the specific fiqh of transforming raisins into a beverage through a process of boiling and significant reduction, a method relevant to pre-modern preservation techniques. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms its permissibility, claring that the extraction of flavor and subsequent concentration does not render the drink impure or prohibited, provided the final product is consumed within the specified timeframe. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly approach to evaluating food preparation methods based on the integrity of the base ingredient rather than the mechanical process of reduction.
